Package common.hardware.camera

Class DynamicCamera

java.lang.Object
common.hardware.camera.DynamicCamera
public class DynamicCamera extends Object
A PhotonVision camera that spots AprilTags and works out where the robot is on the field.

Every loop, periodic() reads each camera's new results, throws out targets that are too far, too close or too uncertain, works out the robot's position, and passes it to the drivetrain to blend into its odometry: 


 frontCamera = new DynamicCamera("FRONT",
     new Transform3d(0.3, 0, 0.5, new Rotation3d(0, Math.toRadians(-20), 0)), // where it is on the robot
     AprilTagFieldLayout.loadField(AprilTagFields.k2026RebuiltWelded),
     (pose, time) -> swerve.addVisionMeasurement(pose, time));

A camera on a turret is "dynamic": use the constructor that takes the turret's position and angle, and it follows the turret as it turns.

In simulation, each camera sees simulated AprilTags from wherever the robot is (see updateSimulation(Pose2d)), so vision code can be tested without a robot.

    • DynamicCamera

      public DynamicCamera(String cameraName, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Transform3d pivotToCam, edu.wpi.first.apriltag.AprilTagFieldLayout tagLayout, BiConsumer<edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d,Double> estConsumer, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation3d offset, Supplier<edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d> angularOffset)
      A camera on a turret, so it turns with it.
      Parameters:
      cameraName - Its name in PhotonVision
      pivotToCam - Where it is from the turret's pivot, and which way it points, with the turret facing forward
      tagLayout - Where the AprilTags are on this year's field
      estConsumer - Gets each pose estimate and its timestamp
      offset - Where the turret's pivot is from the robot's center, in meters
      angularOffset - The turret's angle right now, counterclockwise from facing forward

  • Method Details

    • periodic

      public static void periodic()
      Reads every camera's new results and sends a pose estimate for each one that has a usable target. Call it every loop, from robotPeriodic().

    • setThresholds

      public void setThresholds(double newMinDistThreshold, double newMaxDistThreshold, double newAmbiguityThreshold)
      Sets which tags to trust. A tag far away or seen at a steep angle gives a less accurate position, so it's often better to ignore it. A picture where no tag passes is ignored. When at least one passes and the camera saw several tags, the estimate from all of them together is used, including tags that didn't pass, since far tags still make it better.
      Parameters:
      newMinDistThreshold - Ignore tags closer than this, in meters
      newMaxDistThreshold - Ignore tags farther than this, in meters
      newAmbiguityThreshold - Ignore tags whose ambiguity is above this, from 0 (certain) to 1 (could be either of two positions); 0.2 is a common choice

    • updateSimulation

      public static void updateSimulation(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d robotPose)
      Moves the simulated cameras to where the robot is, and lets them see the AprilTags from there. Call every loop in simulationPeriodic, before periodic() reads them. The field with what they see is on SmartDashboard under VisionSystemSim-main.
      Parameters:
      robotPose - Where the robot is on the field
